decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits within the firm's core cardboard display know-how, so its own R&D can keep refining it, though its absence from the website in 2020 to 2021 raises some doubt.

The pegboard-back shelf display is a small variation on the firm's core competence that its design staff can adapt to customer feedback, but its lack of visibility since 2019 makes a withdrawal more likely.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a core format built directly on existing knowledge and production capacity, so it is the most likely of the products to be maintained.

Wood lies outside the firm's paper-based knowledge base, which limits its ability to learn from results and improve the product, and the product has not been visible since 2019, so its resources are better returned to the cardboard core.
Despite the familiar cardboard know-how, demand from the media segment appears to be shrinking and the product has not been visible since 2019, so its resources are better used in core displays.
